clue.text: Robs the crippled-there's no advantage in this

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them in the street
game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A heartless thief preys on the disabled, and gets nothing for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A mug's game is an idiom for a pursuit that is pointless or unrewarding. 'the' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is any activity that only a fool would take on, since nothing is gained from it.

clue.text: Crazy plan aide entertained

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to hold them within, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: a map is a plan or chart
ADC is aide-de-camp, an officer's assistant

explanation.surface: A ridiculous scheme is put up while an assistant is being hosted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crazy' leads, but the plan is the outer piece; ADC (aide-de-camp) is a military officer's personal assistant.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes wildly reckless or eccentric behaviour.

clue.text: Get request in for seal

indicators.note: the request word is placed inside the word get

parts.note: to ask is to request

explanation.surface: Someone files a request to obtain a seal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasket is a ring or sheet that seals a joint in an engine or pipe.

clue.text: List of explanations from Gary when admitting defeat

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the name takes another word inside it

parts.note: a defeat is a loss

explanation.surface: A reference list is drawn up by Gary as he concedes defeat.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings, usually at the back of a book.

clue.text: Assemble fitting

explanation.surface: An assembly that is appropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather together is to come together for a meeting; meet as an adjective is an old word for suitable or proper.

clue.text: Lousy actor, gets this from critics?

definitions.text: Lousy actor, gets this from critics?

parts.words: Lousy actor, gets this from critics?
parts.note: a bad actor is a ham, and critics may give a performance a severe beating in print; the word joins the bad actor to the verb for a pasting

explanation.surface: A poor performer wonders what the reviewers will say.
explanation.walkthrough: HAM is a bad actor; to hammer a show is to slate it, so a ham gets a hammering.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer is to criticise harshly, the treatment critics hand out to a ham.

clue.text: Notices about war medals

indicators.note: the notices go around the other word

parts.note: ads are notices or advertisements

explanation.surface: Announcements concerning combat honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Medals are honours given in recognition, so they are awards.

clue.text: Angry girl confused about a song

parts.note: mad can mean angry

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the a
the letters of girl are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A furious girl is muddled about a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' turns GIRL into RIGL, and 'about' puts A inside it to make RIGAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A madrigal is a part-song for several voices, popular in the Renaissance.

clue.text: Solitary Cavalier that supports king

indicators.note: cavalier means offhand and careless, so the letters are treated casually and rearranged

explanation.surface: A lone Cavalier backs the king.
explanation.walkthrough: Cavalier looks like the definition, since Cavaliers were the king's men in the English Civil War, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A royalist is a supporter of the monarchy.

clue.text: Find divorces problematic

indicators.note: something problematic is in trouble, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone finds divorces difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To find something is to come upon it for the first time.

clue.text: Nelson's captain accepting money? Not likely

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so the captain holds the money

parts.note: Thomas Hardy was captain of Nelson's flagship Victory at Trafalgar
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Would Nelson's captain take a bribe? Hardly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kiss me, Hardy' were reputedly Nelson's dying words to his captain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardly means scarcely, as an answer suggesting something is improbable.

clue.text: Mean to give information

explanation.surface: Spiteful in order to inform.
explanation.definitionFit: Low-down describes something base or contemptible; the low-down is the inside facts on a matter.

clue.text: Opposed to a poem

parts.note: a verse is a poem

explanation.surface: Against a piece of poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse to something means having a strong dislike of it.

clue.text: Benevolence created by careful testator

explanation.surface: Kindness shown by a person drafting their will with care.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodwill is kindly feeling; read as two words, a careful testator makes a good will, one that is well drafted.

clue.text: Only a small proportion have mercy

explanation.surface: Mercy is shown sparingly.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter is one part in four; to give quarter is to spare a defeated enemy's life.

clue.text: Discarded part of coffee estate

explanation.surface: Coffee dregs from a country estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee grounds are the sediment thrown away after brewing; grounds are also the land around a big house.

clue.text: The ordinary people of one state

explanation.surface: Common folk from a single state.
explanation.definitionFit: The masses are ordinary people; Mass is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state.

clue.text: Monk breaks china cup

indicators.note: a broken cup has its pieces scattered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy monk smashes a china cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A Capuchin is a friar of a Franciscan order known for its pointed hood.

clue.text: Trimming of ermine underneath?

parts.note: ermine is the white winter fur of the stoat
underneath means below

explanation.surface: A gown edged with ermine on its lower part.
explanation.definitionFit: A furbelow is a frill or flounce on a dress, a piece of showy ornament.

clue.text: Force through a lot of nonsense, on the nod

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: bull is slang for a load of rubbish
to be on the nod is to doze off

explanation.surface: A measure is rammed through amid nonsense, with nobody really awake.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a plan is to push it through by force, overriding objections.

clue.text: Be up against a word of caution

parts.note: but is the word that introduces a reservation

explanation.surface: Facing up to a warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that abut lie next to each other, sharing a border.

clue.text: Head shaved, and hands trimmed

parts.note: the hands on a ship are its crew
trimmed hair has been cut

explanation.surface: A sailor's head is shaved and the crew's hair trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew cut is a very short, close-cropped haircut.

clue.text: Throw oneself headlong into series of jobs

explanation.surface: Diving headlong into a succession of jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To career is to rush wildly along; a career is a person's working life through its posts.

clue.text: Temple of deity ringed by parking motorists

parts.note: P is the map symbol for parking

indicators.note: the deity is surrounded by the motorists' letters

parts.note: the AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation
a god is a deity

explanation.surface: A temple to a god surrounded by parked cars.
explanation.definitionFit: A pagoda is a tiered tower used as a Buddhist or Hindu temple.

clue.text: Let tender out

indicators.note: out signals that these letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: A tender is put out to let.
explanation.definitionFit: A let property is one leased to a tenant for payment.

clue.text: Danube is flowing, just

indicators.note: the river's running water stirs these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: The Danube flows, and that is all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only' in the surface; it is the definition, meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A just judgement is fair and impartial.

clue.text: Satisfy Poet Laureate with no difficulty

parts.note: PL is a shortened form of Poet Laureate
ease means freedom from difficulty

explanation.surface: The Poet Laureate effortlessly gives satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: To please someone is to give them satisfaction.

clue.text: You once were a little down-at-heel

indicators.note: only a small part of the words is taken

explanation.surface: You were once somewhat shabby.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the archaic form of you, as the object of a verb.

clue.text: Last year's winner is in hospital, not so young

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
older means less young

explanation.surface: Last year's champion, now older, is in hospital.
explanation.definitionFit: The holder of a title is the current champion, the one who won it last time.

clue.text: Tell solicitor to go away-this is the crunch

parts.note: shoo is what you say to tell someone to go away
a tout solicits custom, pestering people to buy

explanation.surface: Someone tells a lawyer to leave at the decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer, but it means one who solicits, a tout.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out is a decisive contest, such as a penalty shoot-out settling a drawn match.

clue.text: Task for another Noah, in Nottinghamshire?

explanation.surface: A second flood requires a fresh boat in an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: A new Noah would need a new ark; Newark-on-Trent is a market town in Nottinghamshire, an English county.

clue.text: As defier of the Conqueror, he takes the prize

parts.note: taken as written
a prize is a reward

explanation.surface: A rebel against William wins the prize.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to William the Conqueror after 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereward led a rebellion in the Fens against the Norman invader William.
